title: Set a steel door's hinges 5 in below the head, 10 in above the floor, middle centred
instruction: This steel door stands on edge, hinge edge up. The red HEAD line is the frame's head rabbet, where the top of the door hangs; the blue FLOOR line is the finished floor below its bottom end. Lengths along the door are to scale: 1 in = 5 mm. Set the three hinge leaves on the hinge edge at the NAAMM/HMMA hinge locations for a hollow metal door, each lying flat, lengthwise along the edge and centred across it, then let go of them.
context: Carpenters and door hardware installers (O*NET 47-2031.00) hang hollow metal (steel) doors with their hinges at fixed locations, '5, 10 and equal': the top hinge 5 in from the frame's head rabbet to the top of the hinge, the bottom hinge 10 in from the finished floor to the bottom of the hinge, any intermediate hinge centred between them. Allegion's Steelcraft knowledge base gives this as the NAAMM/HMMA hollow metal hinge location, and Ives' hang-the-door guide gives the same three. The two ends are measured from different references by different amounts, so a symmetric or evenly spaced layout is wrong at one end or both, and the middle follows from where the end hinges actually are. Here an 80 in door is drawn at 1 in = 5 mm along its edge (400 mm), with 4-1/2 in hinges (22.5 mm) and a 3/4 in undercut (3.75 mm).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Lengths along the door are to scale, 1 in = 5 mm. Five kinds of thing are on the table, all in one fixed layout. (1) Door: a fixed solid block, grey-painted steel (in a real build a grey-painted wooden block screwed to the table serves), 36 mm thick (along x), 400 mm long (along y) and 80 mm tall, standing on the table on one long face with its hinge edge up: x 28.2 to 31.8 cm (centreline x 30.0 cm), y -20.0 to +20.0 cm, edge top 80 mm above the table. Its top end (the head) is at y +20.0 cm, its bottom end at y -20.0 cm. Thickness and height are not to scale. (2) HEAD line: a fixed red vinyl strip 80 mm long (along x, x 26.0 to 34.0 cm), 6 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick, glued to the table across the door's top end, y +20.0 to +20.6 cm: its door-side edge, level with the door's top end, is the frame's head rabbet. (3) FLOOR line: the same in blue across the bottom end, y -20.375 to -20.975 cm: its door-side edge, 3.75 mm (3/4 in, the undercut) past the door's bottom end, is the finished floor. (4) Parts tray: a fixed dark grey ABS plastic plate 60 x 320 x 3 mm on the table, centred at x 20.0 cm, y 0 (x 17.0 to 23.0 cm, y -16.0 to +16.0 cm). (5) Three hinge leaves: loose solid brass blocks 22.5 mm long, 16 mm wide and 10 mm thick, 31 g each, all faces alike, standing for a folded 4-1/2 in hinge (leaf and knuckle). Each lies flat on the tray with its 22.5 mm side along y, centred at x 20.0 cm and y +13.0 cm, +5.0 cm and -13.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from the leaves' poses (in a real trial: a ruler along the edge from each line's door-side edge, and a photo). A leaf is 'on the edge' when: released (in a real trial: no finger has touched it in the last 0.5 s; in simulation: no gripper's pad-tip point, the point midway between its finger tips, has been within the fingers' reach of the leaf's centre, over every yaw (79 mm fully open, 56.5 mm at a 44 mm opening), and less than 10 mm above its top at any time in the last 0.5 s); settled (its centre moved at most 2 mm and its long side turned at most 1 degree over the last 0.5 s); flat (big faces within 5 degrees of level, either face up); lengthwise (its 22.5 mm side within 5 degrees of the door's length, either way round); resting on the edge (lowest point within 3 mm of the edge top); centred across it (centre within 8 mm of the edge's centreline, so all of it is on the edge even when turned or tilted 5 degrees); and wholly within the door's length. Locations, by the leaf's centre along the door (y), each within 5 mm (1 in): top, its top 25 mm (5 in) below the HEAD line, centre y +163.75 mm; bottom, its bottom 50 mm (10 in) above the FLOOR line, centre y -142.5 mm; middle, centred between the top and bottom leaves. With three leaves on the edge, the highest is the top leaf, the lowest the bottom leaf, and the middle is judged against the midpoint of those two as placed, right or wrong. With fewer than three on the edge, each leaf is judged against the nominal windows, the middle at y +10.625 mm; the windows do not overlap, so a leaf counts for one location at most. k is the number of locations right (0 to 3). First match wins: three leaves on the edge, k = 3, all three settled in each of the last two 0.5 s windows (still for 1 s): 1.0. Three on the edge with the top and bottom both right: 0.75 (the middle off centre, or the 1.0 layout not yet still for 1 s). k = 2: 0.5. k = 1: 0.25. Otherwise 0. Examples: the correct layout 1.0; the middle 10 mm off 0.75; top and bottom right with the third leaf left on the tray 0.5; the bottom copied from the top (symmetric, y -163.75 mm) 0.5; leaves at the quarter points (y +100, 0, -100 mm) 0.25; a leaf still gripped, crosswise, tilted, stacked on another, overhanging a face or off the door counts for nothing; nothing moved 0. Any leaf may go at any location. The trial ends early once the 1.0 state has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit, 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz). A simulator state with a non-finite number scores 0 for that step.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, default friction; the door, lines and tray are fixed. The hinges are solid brass blocks laid on the edge, not leaves mortised and screwed into it. The door is 36 mm thick and 80 mm tall, not to scale, and the 1/8 in head clearance is ignored; only lengths along the edge are to scale. The 5 mm windows are 1 in at full size, looser than a hinge template but far tighter than the 4 to 13 in errors of symmetric or evenly spaced layouts.
reset_notes: Lay the three brass leaves back flat on the tray, their 22.5 mm sides along y, centred at x 20.0 cm and y +13.0, +5.0 and -13.0 cm (any leaf on any spot). The door, the two lines and the tray are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
